A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LinkAlign and support reliable comparison. All pages, appendices, tables, equations, and embedded figures were readable; relocated material could be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original schema-linking experiments, component ablations, a 500-example error analysis, and LinkAlign results on Spider 2.0-lite.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and additionally reports SQL-execution comparisons and measurements of runtime for each framework stage.

M1.justification: v3 Section 4.2.2 introduces a simplified configuration retaining only schema parsing and omitting retrieval and filtering for small-scale SQL generation. The main three-stage framework and Pipeline/Agent strategies remain; fuller descriptions of existing agents do not independently establish a redesign.

E1.justification: v3 extends LinkAlign evaluation on Spider-dev and Bird-dev from schema linking to complete SQL generation. Spider, Bird, AmbiDB, and Spider 2.0-lite remain the datasets used, and the appendix descriptions of dataset construction are unchanged.

E2.justification: The Spider 2.0-lite comparison adds Spider-Agent+Claude-3.7 and removes Spider-Agent+o1-preview and SFT CodeS-15B. The original schema-linking comparator sets remain unchanged. New SQL comparisons in Tables 4–5 include DIN-SQL, MAC-SQL, DAIL-SQL, MCS-SQL, and, on Bird, RSL-SQL.

E3.justification: v3 adds SQL tests using DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen-72B with the first two stages omitted, a DeepSeek-R1 Spider 2.0-lite configuration, and average stage-runtime measurements. These extend the evaluation settings; the original schema-linking metrics, embedding model, and retrieval top-K remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 6 add an efficiency analysis comparing Pipeline and Agent latency for each stage. The original component ablations, their plotted results, and the appendix error analysis are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new runtime table gives averages without adding uncertainty estimation or repeated-run information.

E6.justification: Spider 2.0-lite results change from DeepSeek-V3 at 15.17 and Qwen-Plus at 7.68 in v1 to DeepSeek-V3 at 24.86 and newly reported DeepSeek-R1 at 33.09 in v3. Tables 4–6 add SQL-execution and runtime results, including DeepSeek-V3 EX of 88.9 on Spider-dev and 57.5 on Bird-dev. Original schema-linking and ablation scores remain unchanged; fully matched settings for the revised leaderboard results are not established.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, schema definitions, and evaluation-metric definitions are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs; expanded methodological explanations do not introduce new formal reasoning.

C1.justification: v1 claims leadership excluding long-chain-of-thought reasoning models and reports fourth place overall. v3 instead claims overall Spider 2.0-lite leadership at 33.09 using open-source LLMs, qualified by submission time. This substantially strengthens the headline performance claim while retaining the framework and AmbiDB contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explains omitting retrieval and filtering when schemas fit the context and redundant schema noise is limited. It also adds a rationale for preserving original-query intent during rewriting to reduce hallucination-induced drift. The explicit limitations and most interpretations of the original ablations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds details on metadata serialization, structured query triplets and audit reports, pseudo-SQL validation, adaptive retrieval-round counts, and the evaluation tool. It specifies additional model configurations and sizes. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the retained experiments; the code link and appendix construction instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work text and bibliography are retained, with Related Work moved to Appendix A. Competitive positioning shifts toward an open-source framework competing with proprietary ReFoRCE and Spider-Agent configurations, replacing the earlier emphasis on leadership within the non-long-CoT subset.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, methodology, and experimental narrative. It moves Related Work into the appendix, separates schema-linking and SQL-generation results, and adds a runtime section. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: The opening performance bar chart becomes a leaderboard table with an open-source column. New SQL-execution and stage-runtime tables expand the empirical presentation, while the appendix leaderboard screenshot is removed. The framework diagram, ablation plots, error-distribution figure, and original result tables are retained with changed numbering or placement.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's qualitative efficiency discussion, v3 provides measured stage runtimes and clearer descriptions of agent operations, making the framework easier to assess. New SQL-execution results add useful evidence, but different model backbones prevent clean attribution to LinkAlign, and the stated 6.7%/7.2% gains are not clearly reconciled with Tables 4–5. The net quality improvement is therefore limited.
